mainKeyword: pressure washer for patios and decks
guideTitle: Best Pressure Washers for Patios and Decks (2026)
metaTitle: Best Pressure Washers for Patios and Decks
metaDescription: Six pressure washers for patios, decks and walkways compared by rated flow, pressure control and surface-cleaner readiness, with notes on wood versus concrete.
expertTake: The Westinghouse WPX3400e is the best pick for most patios and decks because its 3000 rated PSI cleans concrete and its pressure can be backed off for wood. The Greenworks 2000 is the value pick for a mostly wooden deck where gentleness matters more than speed. Anyone eyeing the giant 4000 and 4200 PSI listings should read the rating math in this guide first, since the numbers on those boxes do not hold together.
introParagraphs: A patio and a deck are neighbours but need opposite treatment. Concrete and pavers shrug off high pressure and reward flow, because the job is covering a large flat area quickly, while wood punishes anything aggressive and is easily fuzzed, gouged or scarred by a narrow tip or the wrong angle.

The right machine therefore offers enough flow to cover area, enough control to back the pressure down, and ideally the ability to take a surface cleaner attachment for flat work. The headline pressure figure matters least of all.

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3400e brushless electric pressure washer
products.description:
The WPX3400e is the strongest electric here that tells you what it delivers working: 3000 PSI at 1.1 GPM, about 3,300 cleaning units. That much rated pressure lifts ground-in grime from concrete and pavers in a way the 2000 PSI machines cannot, while the pressure drops easily under a wide tip for wood.

The weak point is flow. At 1.1 GPM rated, a large patio is a slow job, and a surface cleaner attachment, which spins a rotary head over flat concrete for even results, needs adequate flow to turn properly, so check the attachment's minimum before you buy one. Against the gas machine in this guide, the electric is quieter, starts at a button and needs no fuel, though it covers ground far more slowly. Against the Greenworks 2000, it brings a clear pressure advantage for stains.

For wood, use a 25 or 40 degree tip, keep the wand moving with the grain and stay about a foot from the surface, testing a hidden board first. Drain the pump after use and before freezing weather. The true brushless motor and auto-stop pump are maintenance-free if kept free of grit.
products.bestFor: Mixed patios and decks where concrete needs real pressure and wood needs it dialed back.
pros: 3000 rated PSI lifts stains from concrete
Pressure backs off easily for wood with wide tips
True brushless motor with auto-stop pump
Clearly states rated output
cons: 1.1 GPM rated flow is slow on big patios
May be too strong for soft wood if misused

products.name: Greenworks 2000 PSI electric pressure washer, PWMA rated
products.description:
For a wood deck, 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM is closer to the right target than a bigger machine, and Greenworks says it was rated to PWMA standards, which at least ties the figures to a common test. At about 2,400 cleaning units it is gentle enough that a wide tip is hard to misuse.

The maker positions it for patio furniture, grills, walkways and vehicles, and a modest deck is a natural extension of that. It lacks the headroom to tackle old oil stains on concrete, which is where the WPX3400e earns its place. Compared with the ePX3500, it states less about the motor and pump, while costing less.

Wood needs careful technique more than power: wet the boards, apply cleaner at low pressure and let it dwell, then rinse with the grain using a 40 degree tip. Drain the pump after each use, avoid kinks in the hose and store the machine indoors in winter.
products.bestFor: Wood decks and light patio cleaning where gentleness matters more than speed.
pros: 2000 PSI is a safe level for most wood
Rated to PWMA standards
Simple and low maintenance
Good for patio furniture and walkways
cons: Not enough headroom for old stains on concrete
1.2 GPM is slow on a big patio

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3500 compact electric pressure washer
products.description:
At 19 pounds and 16.5 inches tall, the ePX3500 is the easiest to carry up to a deck and drag around a patio, and the onboard 20-ounce soap tank means you can apply wood cleaner at low pressure without extra hardware. The rated output of 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM matches the Greenworks 2000 on paper but with clearer documentation.

The rated numbers keep it in the gentle category, so it suits wood decks, composite boards and pavers rather than heavily stained concrete. Against the WPX3400e it is lighter and cheaper but gives up 1000 PSI of rated pressure, and against the Sun Joe SPX100-GO it lists a rated rather than a peak figure.

The braided nylon hose coils easily. Keep the quick-connect o-rings healthy, drain the pump before freezing weather, and flush the soap tank after each use so detergent does not harden inside it.
products.bestFor: Decks and patios up high or far from the hose where a light cart with built-in soap helps.
pros: About 19 lb and easy to carry up steps
Onboard soap tank for low-pressure cleaner
Rated 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM is clear
Braided hose coils easily
cons: Not strong enough for stubborn concrete stains
Soap tank is small for a large deck

products.name: Sun Joe SPX100-GO 1800 PSI compact electric washer
products.description:
This is a small machine for small outdoor spaces: a 13 amp motor with 1800 PSI max and 1.7 GPM max, plus a 13.53-ounce onboard foam bottle for applying detergent. The maker compares its output to 25 times that of a 70 PSI garden hose, a fair description of a light-duty rinse.

Both maxima apply at different settings, so do not multiply them for a cleaning-unit figure. It is the gentlest machine in this guide, which suits a composite or softwood deck and a small paver patio. For concrete with set-in stains it lacks the punch of the WPX3400e.

Use the foam bottle at low pressure on wood and let it dwell, then rinse with a wide tip. Rinse the bottle and drain the pump after use, and keep the cord clear of puddles. Always plug into a GFCI-protected outlet when working on a wet deck, and wear shoes with grip, since a soapy board is slippery. Light and cheap to store, it makes sense for a balcony or a small patio.
products.bestFor: Small patios, balconies and composite decks where a light foam-and-rinse machine is enough.
pros: Compact and portable
Onboard 13.53 oz foam bottle
1800 PSI max is gentle on soft surfaces
13 amp motor draws a standard outlet
cons: Peak figures are not working output

products.name: Steupoek gas pressure washer, 212cc engine, 4200 PSI 4.0 GPM claimed
products.description:
A gas machine is the right tool for a large concrete patio, because flow decides how fast the area gets cleaned, and this listing claims 4.0 GPM from a 212cc engine. That is exactly why it deserves a hard look: 4200 PSI at 4.0 GPM needs about 9.8 hp of hydraulic power, and the engine is listed as 7 hp, so the two claims cannot both be true at the same moment.

The realistic reading is that the machine runs at a lower pressure, or a lower flow, or both, than the box says, much like the Westinghouse electrics list a max that only applies at one setting. It may still clean concrete well, but do not buy it expecting what the label promises, and check the pump and engine brand against your budget. Against the Westinghouse WPX3400e, it offers more potential flow with far more risk of disappointment.

If you buy it, treat it as a regular small-engine machine: change the oil, use fresh stabilized fuel, check the air filter and plug, and protect the pump by never running it dry. Winterize by draining it or running pump antifreeze. Use hearing and eye protection.
products.bestFor: Large concrete patios where flow matters and the buyer accepts the rating uncertainty.
pros: Gas engine delivers high flow for big areas
Five nozzles included
Does not depend on an outlet
Suits large concrete jobs
cons: Pressure and flow claims exceed what a 7 hp engine can supply
Loud, with fuel, oil and winterizing upkeep

products.name: POXURIO electric pressure washer, 4000 PSI 2.8 GPM claimed, 35-ft hose

specList.label: Extras
specList.value: Foam cannon and Total Stop System

products.description:
On paper this is the most powerful electric in the guide, with a foam cannon, a 35-foot hose, a Total Stop System that shuts the machine off when you release the trigger, and three ways to take in water. The claims are the problem: 4000 PSI at 2.8 GPM is about 6.5 hp of hydraulic power, or nearly 4.9 kilowatts, while a standard 15 amp, 120V outlet supplies under 1.8 kilowatts.

That gap means the printed figures are peaks that cannot be sustained or are simply inflated, and the machine will behave more like the 1800 to 2500 PSI class. The accessories may still be useful: the long hose and cannon help on a deck, and the stop system saves wear. Against the Westinghouse WPX3400e, it lacks a stated rated output and a recognizable brand behind it.

If you buy one, test it early, keep the receipt, flush the cannon and drain the pump after each use. Use wide tips on wood and let the cleaner dwell, and assume its real working output is far below the label. A useful check is to compare how a known garden-hose rinse and the machine behave on the same piece of concrete, so you can judge for yourself what the jet actually does before trusting it near wood.
products.bestFor: Decks where the accessories matter more than the label, and the buyer will treat the numbers skeptically.
pros: 35-foot hose and foam cannon included
Total Stop System shuts off on trigger release
Three water-intake methods
Easy assembly
cons: Claimed output exceeds what a household outlet can supply
No stated rated figure and thin brand support

buyingCriteria.explanation: Concrete and pavers are an area job, so flow matters as much as pressure. The Steupoek claims 4.0 GPM against 1.1 rated on the WPX3400e and 1.2 on the ePX3500. A surface cleaner attachment needs enough flow to turn, so check the minimum before buying one.

Soft woods fuzz and gouge above roughly 1500 PSI at the surface with a narrow tip. Use a 25 to 40 degree tip, stay a foot away and move with the grain. The Greenworks 2000 and Sun Joe SPX100-GO sit in the gentle range.

Hydraulic horsepower is PSI times GPM divided by 1,714. The Steupoek's 4200 PSI at 4.0 GPM needs about 9.8 hp, more than the 7 hp it lists, and the POXURIO's 4000 PSI at 2.8 GPM needs about 4.9 kW from an outlet that supplies under 1.8 kW. Treat such claims as marketing.
Westinghouse lists rated output beside peak: 3000 PSI at 1.1 GPM against 3400 max on the WPX3400e, and 2000 at 1.2 against 2500 on the ePX3500. Rated figures are what the machine does under load.
Wood decks respond better to a cleaner that dwells than to pressure. The ePX3500 has a 20-ounce tank and the SPX100-GO a foam bottle. Apply at low pressure, let it work and rinse with the grain.

A machine you carry up deck stairs should be light. The ePX3500 weighs about 19 pounds, while a gas unit like the Steupoek is far heavier. Consider the hose length too, since a 35-foot hose spares you moving the unit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rating plausibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked each machine's claimed PSI and GPM against the hydraulic horsepower formula and its stated motor or engine. The Steupoek and POXURIO claims exceeded what their power sources can supply. This is analysis from specifications, not bench work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Concrete performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at rated pressure and flow, since a large patio needs both. The WPX3400e's 3000 rated PSI scored highest among machines with honest ratings. Flow limited every electric.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wood safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at whether pressure could be backed off and which tips are supplied. The Greenworks 2000 and Sun Joe SPX100-GO scored well for gentleness. Machines with wide tips and soap options scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared weights and hose lengths, from the 19-pound ePX3500 to the heavy gas unit. A light cart helps with stairs and a long hose helps on large decks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed pump type, winterizing and engine care. Electrics are low maintenance, while the gas machine needs oil, fuel and filters.

cards.label: Wand
cards.text: Works on any machine and suits decks, stairs and edges. On big concrete it leaves stripes and takes longer, but it is the only option for wood.

cards.label: Surface cleaner
cards.text: A rotary head covers flat concrete evenly and faster. It needs adequate flow to spin, so it pairs better with the gas machine or the WPX3400e than with the 1.1 GPM models.

howToChoose.note: Use a wand on wood and an add-on surface cleaner on large flat concrete.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A machine whose pressure you can limit, wide tips and a low-pressure soap option. Test on a hidden board and move with the grain.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 2000 and Sun Joe SPX100-GO are gentlest, and the ePX3500 adds an onboard soap tank. The WPX3400e can be used with a wide tip but needs care.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a large concrete patio or stubborn stains. The WPX3400e or a gas machine saves hours.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your project is a small deck or patio. The Greenworks 2000 or SPX100-GO is plenty.

maintenance.interval: After each use and before freezing
maintenance.why: Trapped water can freeze and crack the pump.
A small engine under load needs fresh oil.

maintenance.task: Flush soap from tanks and cannons
maintenance.why: Dried cleaner clogs orifices and fittings.
Hose and fittings are the commonest failure points. Replace worn seals.
A dry pump overheats in seconds. Purge air before pulling the trigger.

faq.q: How much pressure for a wood deck?
faq.a: About 1500 PSI or less at the surface, with a 25 to 40 degree tip held a foot away. A machine rated around 2000 PSI works when used gently.

faq.q: Is higher PSI better for concrete?
faq.a: Higher rated PSI lifts stains, but flow decides how fast a large area is cleaned. A surface cleaner needs enough flow to spin.
The labels usually are not. A standard outlet supplies under 1.8 kilowatts, and 4000 PSI at 2.8 GPM needs about 4.9 kilowatts, so the figure cannot be sustained.

faq.q: Do I need a surface cleaner?
faq.a: For big flat concrete, yes: it is faster and leaves no wand stripes. For decks and stairs a wand is better.

faq.q: Should I use cleaner on a deck?
faq.a: Yes, a wood cleaner applied at low pressure and allowed to dwell does most of the work. Rinse with the grain.

faq.q: Can I use a gas washer on a deck?
faq.a: You can, with wide tips and care, but gas machines make it easy to damage wood. An electric machine around 2000 PSI is a safer fit.
